text: It is conceivable that concurrent training negatively affects growth in other ways. For one, acute factors associated with aerobic training may interfere with resistance training capacity. Specifically, aerobic exercise can cause residual fatigue, substrate depletion, or both, which ultimately impairs the quality of the resistance training bout (31). Muscular adaptations are predicated on the capacity to train with an intensity of effort that sufficiently stimulates myofiber growth. If this ability is compromised, muscular gains necessarily suffer.
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
chapter: Chapter 6: Role of Aerobic Training in Hypertrophy
